title: Loan-to-Value Test Sheet: Curtailment After a Unit Leaves an Equipment & Vehicle Loans Loan
content:
**Computation.** The curtailment on an Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan is the amount by which the principal balance exceeds the product's loan-to-value limit after release, taken as a percentage of the pledged value of the units still securing the loan, rounded to cents; when the principal is within that limit no curtailment is owed.

## Inputs and their records

| Input | Record it is read from |
|---|---|
| Principal balance | the loan record on the test date, after the release proceeds of the day are applied |
| Pledged value of the units still securing the loan | the pledged value of every unit pledged to the loan less that of every unit since released, the unit released that day included among the released |
| Loan-to-value limit after release | the product's figure in the collateral desk schedule |

## The figure, stated as a definition

The permitted principal is the pledged value of the units still securing the loan multiplied by the loan-to-value limit after release and divided by 100. The curtailment is the principal balance less the permitted principal, rounded to cents, and is zero when the principal balance does not exceed the permitted principal.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs, Used Equipment Loan, limit 75 percent)

| Principal balance | Value still pledged | Permitted principal | Curtailment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 80000.00 | 100000.00 | 75000.00 | 5000.00 |
| 75000.00 | 100000.00 | 75000.00 | none (within the limit) |
| 61234.56 | 80000.00 | 60000.00 | 1234.56 |

## Points of judgement

- A principal exactly equal to the permitted principal is within the limit; nothing is owed.
- The test looks at this loan alone: its own principal against its own remaining pledged value.
